history:agent1qdqt3qf6ya54vns92cvzgrs2j0.content:
Here's the success heatmap across all 192 simulated grasps (object × scenario):



**What it shows:**
- **Drop is the universal failure mode** — 0% success for every object, so grip timing/release is the weak point, not force control.
- **Crush and light_grip are mostly fine** — SafeGrip-style force limiting handles crush well (ball, bottle, sponge at 88–100%), and light grips only hurt fragile items (egg 62%, bottle 0%).
- **Nominal is surprisingly shaky** — cup (38%), egg (38%), can and sponge (50%) fail half the time even in the easy case, so there's headroom beyond the extreme scenarios.
- **Hardest cell:** ball in drop (0%). **Easiest:** ball in crush (100%).

Note: these are simulated recordings (dermis-sim-v1), not hardware sessions yet.

**Next steps:**
- I can split this heatmap by SafeGrip on/off to see how much the force limiter rescues crush/light_grip cells.
- Or drill into the nominal failures (cup, egg) — likely slip or early_release — with per-episode analysis.

Here's the outcome breakdown across all 192 simulated grasps:



| Outcome | Episodes | Share |
|---|---|---|
| success | 101 | 53% |
| early_release | 39 | 20% |
| fracture | 32 | 17% |
| incomplete | 10 | 5% |
| slip | 9 | 5% |
| impact | 1 | 1% |

**What it shows:**
- **Success is only 53%** — barely over half the dataset ends in a clean grasp.
- **early_release (20%) and fracture (17%) dominate the failures** — together they're ~75% of all bad outcomes, pointing at release timing and force limiting as the two big problems.
- **Slip is rare (5%)** — the tactile sensing itself seems to detect contact well; it's the grip policy that fails, not the sensing.
- **impact (1 episode)** is a near-non-issue in simulation.

Note: simulated data (dermis-sim-v1), not hardware sessions yet.

**Next steps:**
- Split this pie by SafeGrip on/off to see how much the force limiter cuts the fracture share.
- Or a pie per object (e.g. egg vs sponge) to see which items drive the fracture count.
